**Evaluation of the dash pose:**

**1) Front leg extended / planted — PARTIALLY YES**
The front (right) leg is reaching forward and low, with the foot close to the walkway line (~y≈420–430). However, the foot appears to hover just at/above the surface rather than being firmly planted — the contact reads a bit soft. It's extended toward the ground, but the "planted" feel is weaker than ideal for a lunge frame.

**2) Rear leg trailing, raised — YES**
The rear (left) leg kicks back and up behind the body with a visible bend, clearly off the ground. Combined with the forward-lean torso and motion streak ghosts on the left, the trailing-leg lunge read is solid. The semi-transparent ghost figures behind the player also reinforce the forward momentum.

**3) Shadow / contact core — PARTIAL**
There is a **reflection** of the player on the glossy walkway (visible mirrored figure + sword below), which grounds the character, but a distinct **dark contact shadow blob** directly under the feet is weak/ambiguous — it blends into the dark floor and the reflection does most of the grounding work. A tighter, darker elliptical shadow under the planted foot would improve the "weight on ground" read.

**4) Knee orientation — YES, CORRECT**
Both knees bend forward (toward the direction of travel): the front knee is flexed forward over the reaching foot, and the rear knee points forward/down as the leg trails. No backwards-bending knee artifacts on the main silhouette. (Minor caveat: the overlapping ghost frames make one of the trailing stick-figure legs look slightly ambiguous, but the primary player figure reads correctly.)

**Verdict:** Dash reads well overall — trailing leg, forward lean, knees, and ghost trails are all correct. Main improvements: firm up the front-foot ground contact and add a distinct dark contact shadow (currently relying on the reflection alone).
